articles.title: Veterans charity says demand for support is growing after emotional day for volunteers
articles.excerpt: A Rochdale organisation supporting military veterans and disadvantaged young people has issued an emotional appeal for greater support after a recent case reminded volunteers why their work remains so important.
articles.content_html:
A Rochdale-based community organisation supporting military veterans and disadvantaged young people has issued an emotional appeal for greater public support after what it described as one of the most challenging days in its history.

Get Together After Serving CIC (GTAS) said a recent case involving people it was assisting left members of its leadership team deeply affected, highlighting the growing pressures facing both former servicemen and women and vulnerable children within the community. While the organisation has not released details of the case in order to protect those involved, it says the experience reinforced the urgent need for the support services it provides every day.

In a heartfelt statement shared with supporters, GTAS explained that one of its directors, Wayne, was left visibly emotional after witnessing the circumstances surrounding the latest referral. According to the organisation, despite a lifetime of experience dealing with trauma, military service and personal hardship, the situation served as a powerful reminder that many people continue to struggle in silence.

The organisation says these moments rarely become public. Instead, staff and volunteers often work quietly behind the scenes, providing practical assistance, emotional support and signposting to those who find themselves in crisis. GTAS says much of its work takes place away from social media and public attention, with the focus remaining firmly on helping individuals rather than seeking recognition.

Founded to support former members of the Armed Forces while also creating opportunities for disadvantaged children and young people, Get Together After Serving CIC has steadily expanded its role within the local community. Alongside offering companionship and welfare support for veterans, the organisation works to reduce social isolation, improve wellbeing and create positive opportunities for young people who may otherwise feel overlooked.

Veterans' charities across the UK have repeatedly highlighted the complex challenges many former service personnel face after leaving the Armed Forces. Although the transition to civilian life is smooth for many, others experience difficulties relating to housing, employment, mental health, financial hardship or adjusting to life outside military service. Community organisations often play an important role by offering early intervention before problems escalate.

At the same time, many charities supporting children and young people have reported increasing demand for services as families continue to face financial pressures and wider social challenges. Community groups such as GTAS frequently rely on volunteers, donations and fundraising to continue delivering projects that might otherwise be unavailable to those who need them.

GTAS says its work demonstrates how relatively small organisations can have a significant impact despite operating with limited resources. Its latest appeal emphasises that a dedicated team of volunteers continues to provide support every day because they believe nobody should have to face hardship alone.

In its statement, the organisation said the latest events reinforced its belief that its work is not simply beneficial but, in some cases, life-changing. It described helping veterans find safety and dignity while giving disadvantaged young people opportunities, stability and a place where they feel valued.

The charity is now encouraging local residents, businesses and community organisations to become involved, whether by volunteering, making donations, fundraising or simply helping raise awareness of its work. It believes that increasing community support will allow it to reach more people before problems become crises.

Like many community interest companies, GTAS operates in an increasingly challenging funding environment. Demand for grassroots support services has grown while competition for grants and charitable funding has become more intense. As a result, many organisations rely heavily on local goodwill to sustain their work.

The latest appeal serves as a reminder that behind every public fundraising campaign or social media post are real people facing difficult circumstances, often away from public view. For the volunteers involved, success is not measured by headlines or recognition but by the number of people who receive help when they need it most.

Anyone wishing to learn more about Get Together After Serving CIC, volunteer their time or support its work can find further information through the organisation's social media channels. GTAS says every contribution, no matter how small, helps strengthen its ability to support veterans and young people across the Rochdale area.

articles.title: New Initiative Launched to Connect Young People with Activities
articles.excerpt: A new programme called Young Peoples Activity Search aims to engage youth in Rochdale by providing a comprehensive list of local activities and opportunities for participation.
articles.content_html:
A new programme called Young Peoples Activity Search has been launched to connect young people with various activities in Rochdale. The initiative aims to provide a comprehensive list of opportunities for youth engagement and participation.

This programme is part of the REACH project, which focuses on enhancing community involvement and promoting positive activities for young people.

Details about specific activities and how to get involved can be found on the Rochdale REACH website.

The initiative is expected to encourage more young people to participate in local events and activities, fostering a sense of community and belonging.

articles.title: Rochdale's Future Masterplan Advances Towards Implementation
articles.excerpt: A masterplan aimed at shaping the future of Rochdale is progressing towards realisation, with key developments expected soon.
articles.content_html:
A masterplan that aims to shape the future of Rochdale is moving closer to implementation. The plan, which outlines various developments and improvements for the area, has received significant attention and support.

Local officials have indicated that the next steps in the process will involve further consultations and planning stages. This could lead to tangible changes in the community, impacting infrastructure and local services.

The masterplan is expected to address various aspects of urban development, including housing, transport, and public spaces, which may enhance the quality of life for residents.

As the project progresses, updates will be provided to keep the community informed about upcoming developments and opportunities for involvement.

articles.title: Search for Lost Family Member in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A family member is searching for Kevin Gregory, who is believed to be living in Rochdale. They hope to reconnect after years apart.
articles.content_html:
A person is searching for a lost family member, Kevin Gregory, who was born in 1972 in Macclesfield. The family believes he is currently living in Rochdale.

The individual, who posted on social media, expressed a desire for Kevin to reach out to his mother and grandmother, who would like to know he is doing well.

The family has stated that if Kevin prefers not to be in contact, they will respect his wishes. They hope to reconnect after years apart.

Anyone with information about Kevin Gregory's whereabouts is encouraged to come forward.

articles.title: Community Fun Day in Heywood Attracts Over 450 Residents
articles.excerpt: More than 450 residents attended a community fun day in Heywood, organised by Rochdale Youth Service, featuring free food and various activities.
articles.content_html:
A community fun day held in Heywood attracted more than 450 local residents over the weekend. The event was organised by Rochdale Youth Service and offered a range of free food and activities.

Participants enjoyed various activities, including fun physical sessions, a bouncy castle, henna artistry, and art workshops. The event aimed to foster community spirit and provide entertainment for families.

The fun day provided an opportunity for residents to engage with one another and enjoy a day of leisure and enjoyment. Organisers reported a positive turnout and feedback from attendees.

Such events are likely to continue to promote community engagement and provide a platform for local services to connect with residents.

articles.title: KYP Launches Community Cinema with Screening of Bend It Like Beckham
articles.excerpt: KYP has launched a new Community Cinema with a screening of Bend It Like Beckham, celebrating South Asian Heritage Month and promoting community engagement.
articles.content_html:
KYP has officially launched its new Community Cinema with a screening of the film Bend It Like Beckham, held on 23 July as part of South Asian Heritage Month.

The event welcomed attendees of all ages for an evening celebrating film, culture and community. Guests enjoyed complimentary popcorn, nachos and refreshments before watching the 2002 film, which explores themes of identity, family expectations, friendship, ambition and cultural heritage.

Following the screening, audience members participated in a question and answer session with actress Shaheen Khan, who portrayed Mrs Bhamra in the film. Khan reflected on the film's making, its cultural impact, and the importance of authentic representation in the arts and media. She engaged with the audience, sharing behind-the-scenes stories and discussing how the film continues to inspire audiences more than two decades after its release.

KYP aims to use the Community Cinema to encourage conversation, strengthen community connections and bring together people from diverse backgrounds. The initiative forms part of KYP's wider commitment to promoting inclusion and supporting community cohesion. Organisers plan to hold further screenings throughout the year following the positive response from attendees.

articles.title: Day of Action Held at Baguley Crescent in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A collaborative effort involving local authorities and residents took place at Baguley Crescent in Rochdale on 24th July to address community issues.
articles.content_html:
A day of action was held at Baguley Crescent in Rochdale on 24th July, involving Bury Council, Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS), ward councillors, community partners, and local residents.

The initiative aimed to address various community issues and improve the local environment. Participants engaged in activities designed to enhance safety and community cohesion.

This collaborative effort reflects ongoing commitments by local authorities to work alongside residents in tackling challenges within the area.

Further details on the outcomes of the day of action have not yet been disclosed.

articles.title: Volunteers raise £450 for Christian Aid at Whitworth Skyline Walk breakfast
articles.excerpt: Volunteers from Thrum Hall Methodist Church raised £450 for Christian Aid by serving breakfast to walkers during the Whitworth Skyline Walk.
articles.content_html:
A group of volunteers from Thrum Hall Methodist Church raised £450 for Christian Aid by providing breakfast for participants in the Whitworth Skyline Walk.

The volunteers set up a breakfast stall along the route of the annual event, serving bacon sandwiches and hot drinks to over 500 walkers completing the 14-mile challenge. The walk, organised by Whitworth Sports Council, follows a circular route around the boundary of Whitworth, featuring moorland and varied terrain.

Diane Chadwick, a member of Thrum Hall Methodist Church, expressed satisfaction with the event, stating, "It was a glorious day, and the walkers seemed very pleased with our efforts." She added that the funds raised would support Christian Aid projects delivered by local partners in communities around the world.

The church plans to host another fundraiser, a pamper session with Afternoon Tea, on 26th July. Christian Aid reports that support from fundraisers helps reach vulnerable communities globally, having assisted 4.1 million people through nearly 400 projects between 2024 and 2025.
